I was out on a familiar walk through my neighborhood on a crisp autumn morning. The air was cool and the leaves were turning a stunning range of reds, oranges and yellows. I strolled down my usual route, noting the familiar sights - my neighbor's dog perched on his porch, the usual cars parked in driveways.

As I walked by the old elm tree at the end of the street, something caught my eye. I paused, squinting to get a better look. Nestled between the gnarled branches was a small, silver jewelry box, partially hidden by leaves. 

My heart raced as I wondered who could have left such a thing. I carefully stepped closer, trying not to disturb the fallen foliage. I noticed a small note taped to the box. I peeled it off and read:

"For someone who appreciates beauty. Open me and take what you like."
